entries.answer:
Use the following prompt.[1]

```text
Build a complete, production-ready frontend-only web application as a single self-contained `index.html` file with embedded HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, based on the provided technical description of a sophisticated browser-based visual editing platform. [file:1] Reconstruct the full client-side system from beginning to end, preserving all substantive behaviors, structures, interaction models, interface regions, and editing workflows implied by the source description, while omitting any reference to the original product or service name. [file:1] Do not produce a mockup, prototype, demo, simplified version, placeholder implementation, fake data shell, or partial scaffold. [file:1] Produce the real frontend application architecture in one file, with complete UI, complete state management, complete interaction logic, and complete styling. [file:1]

Construct the application as a dense, modern, professional single-page editor interface intended for creating and editing visual projects in the browser. [file:1] The page must feel like a full web editor rather than a marketing site or dashboard. [file:1] Organize the interface into the major regions implied by the source description: a top toolbar/header area, a central editable workspace or canvas zone, side panels or drawers for tools and properties, modal and overlay systems, contextual popups, bottom or thumbnail navigation regions where appropriate, and responsive mobile-specific adaptations. [file:1] Include the full editing shell, not just isolated widgets. [file:1]

Implement the overall application layout with production-quality responsiveness for desktop and mobile. [file:1] On desktop, the interface must support a multi-region editor composition with persistent tool surfaces, clear panel hierarchy, layered overlays, and a central working area. [file:1] On mobile, transform the layout into touch-friendly stacked or bottom-sheet-based interaction patterns, preserving editor functionality without merely shrinking the desktop layout. [file:1] Use responsive breakpoints, adaptive spacing, and mobile-safe fixed positioning where necessary. [file:1]

Create a complete design system directly inside the file. [file:1] Define CSS custom properties for colors, typography, spacing, corner radii, shadows, z-index layers, motion timings, and component states. [file:1] Include support for light and dark themes, with a working theme toggle implemented in JavaScript and applied via root-level attributes or classes. [file:1] Use polished, application-grade styling with proper visual hierarchy, readable text contrast, layered surfaces, dividers, interactive states, and refined transitions. [file:1]

Implement the application shell so that it includes a professional toolbar/header with actionable controls, project-level actions, navigation affordances, and mode-specific UI states. [file:1] Add left and/or right side panels for tools, assets, settings, and inspector-style controls. [file:1] Add contextual controls that appear based on selection, hover, active state, or editing mode. [file:1] Include bottom-sheet behavior or secondary control surfaces for mobile where the source description indicates mobile-specific editor patterns. [file:1]

Build the central editor/workspace as the primary interaction area. [file:1] It must visually and behaviorally function like an actual editable canvas or project stage rather than a static preview. [file:1] Support selection, focus indication, layer-like manipulation affordances, editable regions, drag-capable interactions where relevant, and visible state changes tied to user actions. [file:1] Maintain internal application state for selected elements, active tool, open panel, modal visibility, theme, viewport mode, and editor context. [file:1]

Create a robust overlay system. [file:1] Include modal dialogs, popovers, tooltips, dropdowns, error overlays, confirmation states, temporary notification surfaces, and contextual action menus as required by the technical description. [file:1] Every overlay must have correct layering, focus handling, dismissal behavior, and visual distinction from the base editor. [file:1] Support multiple overlay types such as full-screen overlays, centered dialogs, anchored menus, and bottom sheets. [file:1]

Implement polished interactive controls throughout the app. [file:1] This includes buttons, icon buttons, segmented controls, tabs, accordions, dropdown selectors, form inputs, text areas, toggle switches, badges, chips, thumbnail frames, cards, and scrollable panels. [file:1] Every interactive element must have hover, focus, active, disabled, and selected states where applicable. [file:1] Use semantic HTML and accessible labeling for all controls. [file:1]

Reconstruct the editor-style behaviors implied by the description rather than only the visible appearance. [file:1] Include stateful panel expansion and collapse, selectable frames or items, contextual placeholder behavior, hidden and revealed action groups, hover-triggered affordances on desktop, alternative touch behavior on mobile, thumbnail or frame scrollers, and active/inactive styling transitions. [file:1] Where the source implies timing-based or eased motion, implement those transitions in JavaScript and CSS so the interface feels operational. [file:1]

Include error, empty, loading, and fallback states as first-class parts of the system. [file:1] Build styled error modals, empty-state panels, skeleton or placeholder loading treatments where appropriate, image/content fallback regions, and disabled interaction states that still look deliberate and finished. [file:1] Do not leave any state visually unhandled. [file:1]

Implement editor-specific navigation structures. [file:1] Include toolbars, back-navigation affordances, project actions, thumbnail/frame navigation, play/preview-related controls if implied by the source, and grouped action containers that can expand, collapse, or animate between compact and detailed states. [file:1] Make these controls behave like a real editing environment with clear mode transitions. [file:1]

Use layered CSS architecture inside the single file. [file:1] Separate base reset styles, theme tokens, layout rules, component rules, utility rules, state classes, and animation definitions within the `<style>` block in a clean, maintainable order. [file:1] Write structured JavaScript in the `<script>` block using modules or well-organized functions and classes, with no dead code and no pseudo-code. [file:1] Keep all logic production-grade and fully wired to the DOM. [file:1]

The JavaScript must initialize the whole interface, bind all events, manage application state, render dynamic regions, and coordinate component behavior. [file:1] Use a clear state model for panels, modals, active canvas item, current tool, theme, responsiveness, and transient UI elements. [file:1] Ensure interactions remain consistent when switching between desktop and mobile layouts. [file:1]

Include keyboard accessibility and interaction quality throughout. [file:1] Support focus visibility, Escape-to-close behavior for overlays, button semantics, label/input associations, and logical tab order. [file:1] Prevent inaccessible click-only patterns when a semantic solution is possible. [file:1] Also ensure touch targets are appropriate for mobile use. [file:1]

The implementation must be visually complete. [file:1] Do not leave unfinished areas, blank panels, unlabeled sections, raw debug text, or nonfunctional decorative controls. [file:1] Every visible region must have purpose, structure, and behavior. [file:1] Any sample project content used inside the editor must be realistic, fully integrated, and sufficient to demonstrate all editing surfaces without using fake or obviously placeholder filler. [file:1]

Do not use external build steps, frameworks that require compilation, or multiple files. [file:1] The entire frontend must run directly by opening `index.html` in a browser. [file:1] If external libraries are needed, load them via CDN only when they materially improve the final production result, and integrate them fully rather than superficially. [file:1] Keep assets inline where possible using SVG, CSS, or embedded data structures so the file remains self-contained. [file:1]

Deliver the final answer as one complete, unabridged `index.html` document only. [file:1] Include all required markup, styles, scripts, editor regions, overlays, controls, responsive behavior, and interaction logic in that single file. [file:1] Output no explanation, no summary, no notes, and no surrounding text outside the final code. [file:1]
```
